headline: Warm-up prepares your body for demands—transitioning from rest to performance gradually
universal_truth: Transitions matter; jumping from rest to peak performance invites failure; gradual ramp-up protects and prepares
fun_facts: Warm muscles are more flexible and less prone to injury than cold muscles
A proper warm-up increases heart rate gradually, preparing the cardiovascular system
Mental warm-ups also exist—athletes visualize before performing
discussion_questions: How do you transition into demanding activities?
What happens when you skip warm-up in different areas of life?
Where could you add preparation phases?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Cold muscles tear. Cold engines stall. You can't go from zero to maximum instantly—bodies and machines both need warm-up. Preparation is the transition from rest to readiness. Skip it and invite failure.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: We often jump straight into demands without preparation. Why does warm-up matter?

options.text: Warm-up gradually shifts systems from rest to performance—increasing blood flow, activating muscles, focusing attention; the transition prevents injury and improves output
options.response: Yes. Cold muscles can't perform like warm ones. The warm-up isn't wasted time—it's essential preparation. Gradual transition protects and prepares. The same principle applies beyond physical activity.
Injury prevention is key, but warm-up also improves performance by preparing all systems...

q1.title: Gradual Transition
q1.script: Warm-up is gradual transition—moving from resting state to performance state step by step. Each stage prepares the next. Rushing the transition invites problems.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Gradual Transition"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: System Activation
q2.script: Warm-up activates systems: blood flows, muscles activate, joints lubricate, focus sharpens. It's not just muscles—it's the whole system preparing for demands.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Life Warm-Ups
q3.script: The principle extends beyond physical: morning routines warm you up for the day. Pre-meeting preparation warms up your thinking. Transitions matter everywhere.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Transitions matter. Jumping from rest to peak performance invites failure. Gradual ramp-up protects and prepares.

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.

growTrack.title: Transition Audit - Where Do You Skip Warm-Up?
growTrack.learning_objective: Identify areas needing better preparation phases
growTrack.activity: Where do you jump straight into demands without warm-up—exercise, work, difficult conversations? What preparation phase could you add? Design a warm-up routine for a demanding activity in your life.
